title: Mass of Earth
description: Essential Criteria: The formula for the mass of the Earth must be correctly stated as m_e = gR^2/G.

title: Mass of Moon
description: Essential Criteria: The equation relating the mass of the moon to the gravitational constant and orbital parameters must be correctly presented as G(m_m + m_e) = 4πa^3/T^2.

title: Distance to Sun
description: Essential Criteria: The method for calculating the distance from the Earth to the Sun must be clearly articulated, including the relevant angles and distances.

title: Key Reasoning
description: Important Criteria: The reasoning behind using gravitational laws and Kepler's laws must be clearly explained.

title: Measurable Quantities
description: Important Criteria: The measurable quantities needed for each calculation must be identified, such as g, R, a, T.

title: Common Errors
description: Pitfall Criteria: Any sign mistakes or incorrect application of gravitational formulas must be avoided.

title: Units Consistency
description: Optional Criteria: Units for all quantities should be consistent and correctly applied throughout the calculations.

title: Limiting Cases
description: Optional Criteria: Discussion of limiting cases or assumptions made in the calculations can enhance the response.
